meta.titre: Synovial Joints: Structure, Types and Movement at the Elbow and Knee
meta.sous_theme: Structure, types and muscle action at freely movable joints

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: When a goalkeeper in Yaounde dives to stop a ball, his shoulder swings in a wide circle while his knees bend and straighten again and again. These movements are possible because of synovial joints, the freely movable joints of the body. Every year the GCE asks for the type of a named joint and for a clear description of how a limb bends and straightens, so you must know the parts of a joint and the work of muscles in pairs.

items: A joint is a place where two or more bones meet.
Muscles contract to pull on bones and cannot push.
Tendons join muscles to bones, and ligaments join bone to bone.

sections.titre: Structure, types and working of synovial joints
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Parts of a synovial joint

| Part | Function |
|---|---|
| Articular cartilage | smooth layer on the bone ends; reduces friction and absorbs shock |
| Synovial membrane | lines the capsule and makes synovial fluid |
| Synovial fluid | lubricates the joint so the bones move smoothly |
| Joint capsule | tough covering that holds the joint together and keeps the fluid in |
| Ligaments | join the bones and prevent the joint from moving too far |

### Types of synovial joint

| Type | Movement | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Ball and socket | in all directions, including rotation | shoulder, hip |
| Hinge | in one plane only, bending and straightening | elbow, knee |
| Pivot | rotation, turning | atlas and axis in the neck |
| Gliding | small sliding movements | between small bones of the wrist |
| Saddle | movement in two directions | base of the thumb |

### Muscles work in pairs
A muscle can only pull, so bones are moved by **antagonistic pairs** of muscles. When one muscle of the pair **contracts**, the other **relaxes**. Muscles contract when they receive nerve impulses and use energy released by respiration. At the elbow, the **biceps** is at the front of the upper arm and the **triceps** is at the back. The biceps is attached by a tendon to the radius and the triceps by a tendon to the ulna.

variantes.nom: Describing movement at a hinge joint (elbow)
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how a limb bends and straightens
variantes.contenu_markdown: To **bend** the arm, the biceps contracts and pulls the radius upwards, while the triceps relaxes. The forearm moves towards the shoulder. To **straighten** the arm, the triceps contracts and pulls the ulna, while the biceps relaxes. The joint can move in one plane only, because it is a hinge joint. Add details to earn marks: the humerus stays fixed, tendons transmit the pull, nerve impulses make the muscles contract, energy comes from respiration, and synovial fluid and cartilage let the bones move without friction.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question describes a joint problem
variantes.contenu_markdown: A **sprain** is the stretching or tearing of ligaments. A **dislocation** is when a bone is pulled out of its normal position in the joint. **Arthritis** is the inflammation of joints, which become painful and stiff.

sections.enonce_markdown: A footballer kicks a ball by straightening his leg at the knee. Describe how the leg is straightened and name the type of joint at the knee. *(6 marks)*

etapes.justification: The command word is "describe", but the type of joint is also asked.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The knee is a hinge joint, so the leg can move in one plane only.

etapes.justification: A limb needs two muscles that pull in opposite directions.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The quadriceps at the front of the thigh and the hamstring muscles at the back of the thigh.

etapes.justification: State which muscle contracts and which relaxes.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The quadriceps contracts and the hamstring muscles relax.

etapes.action: Show how the pull reaches the bone
etapes.justification: Muscles act on bones through tendons.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The quadriceps pulls through its tendon on the tibia (the shin bone), which lifts the lower leg forward.

etapes.justification: Marks are given for the cause of the contraction and for the smooth working of the joint.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Nerve impulses make the muscle contract, using energy from respiration. Synovial fluid and cartilage reduce friction.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The knee is a hinge joint. To straighten the leg, the quadriceps at the front of the thigh contracts, pulls on the tibia through its tendon and straightens the leg, while the hamstring muscles at the back relax. The two muscles are an antagonistic pair, because a muscle can only pull. Nerve impulses cause the contraction, and the energy comes from respiration. Cartilage and synovial fluid reduce friction so the bones move smoothly. To bend the leg again, the hamstring muscles contract and the quadriceps relaxes.

items.erreur_markdown: "To bend the arm, the triceps contracts."
items.pourquoi_faux: Bending the arm at the elbow is done by the biceps. The triceps straightens the arm.
items.correction_markdown: Bending: biceps contracts, triceps relaxes. Straightening: triceps contracts, biceps relaxes.

items.erreur_markdown: "The biceps pulls the arm up and the triceps pushes it down."
items.pourquoi_faux: Muscles never push. They can only pull when they contract, so a second muscle is needed to move the bone back.
items.correction_markdown: The muscles form an antagonistic pair: one contracts while the other relaxes.

items.pourquoi_faux: Synovial fluid is a lubricant. Ligaments and the joint capsule hold the bones in place.
items.correction_markdown: Synovial fluid reduces friction; ligaments join the bones.

items.erreur_markdown: "The shoulder and the elbow are both hinge joints."
items.pourquoi_faux: The shoulder is a ball and socket joint, which moves in all directions. Only the elbow is a hinge joint that moves in one plane.
items.correction_markdown: Shoulder: ball and socket. Elbow: hinge.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the type of synovial joint at each place: (a) the hip, (b) the knee, (c) between the atlas and axis vertebrae, (d) the elbow.
State the function of each: (a) synovial fluid, (b) articular cartilage, (c) a ligament, (d) a tendon.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Synovial fluid **lubricates** the joint and reduces friction.

(b) Articular cartilage is a smooth layer that **reduces friction and absorbs shock**.

(c) A ligament **joins one bone to another** and limits movement.

(d) A tendon **joins a muscle to a bone**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A boy lifts a heavy bucket by bending his arm at the elbow. Later, he twists his ankle badly while running.

(a) Name the muscle that contracts to lift the bucket and say what the triceps does.
(b) Explain why two muscles are needed at the elbow.
(c) The doctor says that ligaments in the ankle are torn. Name this injury.
(d) Explain why a joint with worn cartilage is painful to move.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The **biceps** contracts; the triceps **relaxes**.

(b) A muscle can only pull. One muscle bends the arm, so a second muscle is needed to pull the bone back and straighten the arm again.

(c) A **sprain**.

(d) Cartilage normally makes the bone ends smooth and absorbs shock. When it is worn, the bone ends rub together, causing friction, pain and stiffness.

items_markdown: A synovial joint has articular cartilage, a synovial membrane producing synovial fluid, a capsule and ligaments.
Ball and socket joints (shoulder, hip) move in all directions; hinge joints (elbow, knee) move in one plane; the neck has a pivot joint.
Muscles work in antagonistic pairs: one contracts while the other relaxes, because muscles only pull.
At the elbow, the biceps bends the arm and the triceps straightens it; at the knee, the quadriceps straightens the leg.
A sprain is damage to ligaments; a dislocation is a bone out of position; arthritis is inflammation of joints.
